profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
profile.summary: Software engineer with extensive experience designing, developing, and supporting mission-critical applications that analyze scientific data from spacecraft instruments.  Resourceful problem-solver, adept at rapidly comprehending existing code, and mastering new scientific and technical topics.  Experienced in a wide variety of programming environments: OO (Java, C++), procedural (C, Fortran), scripting (Perl, Python), and web-based (JavaScript) with a particular interest in visualizing complex data and designing intuitive interfaces.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Develop analysis software and scripts for SAM (Sample Analysis at Mars), an instrument on MSL (Mars Science Laboratory) aka Curiosity, including software in a scientific data analysis environment called Igor Pro to monitor the health of the SAM instrument and provide a GUI for scientists on our team to quickly analyze SAM data. Also, developing web-based applications for visualizing SAM housekeeping data using AngularJS and Bootstrap.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: Development of Java applications for particle data analysis, such as a spectrogram viewer for the DMSP SSJ instrument. Development of interactive 3D analysis tools for displaying spacecraft in the context of planetary magnetic fields, and rendering 3D isosurfaces from model data. Data analysis support for EPPS particle detector on the MESSENGER Mercury mission. Development of mobile applications for iOS devices, including an education and public outreach iPhone app for the New Horizons mission, a real-time telemetry-viewing app for the STEREO mission, improvements to a time logging app for a Navy fatigue study, and a GPS routing app for use in a military context.

company.name: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

positions.title: SAM Flight Scripts Engineer
positions.description: The development, validation, and operation of experiment sequence scripts that perform gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) on material delivered to an array of sample cups onboard SAM (Sample Analysis at Mars), an instrument on MSL (Mars Science Laboratory) aka Curiosity.

positions.title: Lead Programmer
positions.description:
Contractor at High Energy Astrophysics Science Archive Research Center (HEASARC)

The development and support of Ximage, an x-ray astronomy imaging analysis application implemented in C, Fortran and Tcl/Tk (>60k lines). Duties included the enhancement (e.g. FITS WCS coordinate system support), maintenance and support (i.e. interacting with customers via email helpline and writing print and web documentation) of the application.

Also, co-architect of Apache/modperl/Mason web application (>10k lines OO Perl, >5k lines HTML/Mason) used by scientists to share data and collaborate. Information arriving via web forms or GPG-encoded e-mail messages populate database tables and become searchable by privileged users.

Responsible for the development, operation and support of a mission-critical Perl script system (>6k lines) which automatically transfers and archives Swift gamma-ray burst data among independent sites in US, UK and Italy. Also, responsible for implementing and automating a suite of scripts, which cross-validate the incoming data against expected structure.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Enhancement of NPAS (Network Planning and Analysis System), an X-Windows application used to conduct TDRSS and ground station loading studies.  Authored test plans and created test beds executed by QA personnel. Assistant editor of newly created NPAS User's Guide (>500 pages) conforming to NASA TIP 2110 document standard. Duties included writing ~1/4 of document, formatting entire document, and creating Word macros for index creation.  Assisted in the analysis of coverage requirements with Satellite Toolkit (STK)
